$schema_comment: Catalog of integrations the user can self-activate. Frontend renders one card per entry. fields[].optional skips the required-check; mcp.envMap maps catalog field names to env-var name the MCP code reads; mcp.inheritEnv lists platform env vars (e.g. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID) to copy from process.env at spawn time. mcp.args supports {appsDir} placeholder so the same catalog works locally and in /opt/ide. mcp.allowedHosts lists every outbound hostname the integration needs at runtime — egress.js writes the active union to /srv/<ide>/egress/allowed-hosts.txt and the host-side egress-allowlist.sh resolves these to ipset entries; values wrapped in {{FIELD}} are substituted from the active store per-tenant (e.g. {{SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN}}, {{EMAIL_HOSTS_RESOLVED}}).

steps.title: Sign in to xAI

steps.title: Create an API key

steps.title: Set a spending cap (recommended)

integrations.description: Chat with the assistant via a Telegram bot. The bot process restarts (~5s) when you activate or remove this.

fields.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
fields.label: Bot token
fields.helper: Format: <bot_id>:<35-char-secret>. Issued by @BotFather.

fields.name: TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID
fields.label: Admin chat ID
fields.helper: Your Telegram numeric user ID. Send /start to @userinfobot to see it.

steps.title: Create the bot with @BotFather
steps.body:
On Telegram, open [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) and send `/newbot`.

- Display name: **{{botDisplayName}}**
- Username: must end with `bot` and be globally unique. Try `{{botName}}_bot`, `{{botName}}bot`, or `{{botName}}_team_bot`.

BotFather replies with a token like `1234567890:AAE...` — paste it as the **Bot token** below.

steps.title: Set a profile picture (optional)
steps.body: Want {{botDisplayName}} to have a face in Telegram? Download one of these and upload it via @BotFather → menu → set bot's photo.

steps.title: Get your admin chat ID
steps.body:
Open [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot) on Telegram and send `/start`.

It replies with your numeric ID — paste it as **Admin chat ID** below. Only this account will be able to chat with {{botDisplayName}}.

steps.title: Add teammates (optional)

fields.name: SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN
fields.label: Store domain
fields.helper: Internal .myshopify.com domain — not your public domain.

fields.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID

fields.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET

steps.title: Create a Shopify dev app
steps.body: Open [dev.shopify.com](https://dev.shopify.com), select your store, click **Create app**. Name it something memorable (e.g. `shopify-mcp`).

steps.title: Add Admin API scopes

- `read/write_customers`
- `read/write_inventory`
- `read/write_orders`
- `read/write_products`
- `read_locations`
- `read/write_fulfillments`
- `read/write_draft_orders`

steps.title: Find your .myshopify.com domain

Look at your Shopify Admin URL: `admin.shopify.com/store/`**`<handle>`**`/...`

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Secret

Go to [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com) → **My Apps** → **Create App** → **Business** type.

- `catalog_management`

fields.name: GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN
fields.label: Developer token
fields.helper: From ads.google.com/aw/apicenter — requires a Manager (MCC) account.

fields.name: GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID
fields.label: Customer ID
fields.helper: Account number without dashes.

fields.name: GOOGLE_ADS_REFRESH_TOKEN
fields.label: OAuth refresh token (optional, for write tools)
fields.helper: Generated once via OAuth consent flow. Skip for read-only access. Uses the platform OAuth client.

steps.title: Get a Developer Token
steps.body:
Open [ads.google.com/aw/apicenter](https://ads.google.com/aw/apicenter) and copy the **Developer Token** (22 alphanumeric chars).

You need a **Manager (MCC) account** for this — without it the token won't work. New tokens start in Test status; apply for **Basic Access** on the same page if you need live data.

steps.title: Enable the Google Ads API
steps.body:
Open [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com) → **APIs & Services** → **Enable APIs** → search **Google Ads API** → **Enable**.

Use the same Cloud project that powers your platform OAuth so Client ID/Secret are reused.

steps.title: Find your Customer ID

[ads.google.com](https://ads.google.com) → top-right of the dashboard shows it.

Strip the dashes — `123-456-7890` becomes `1234567890`.

steps.title: Refresh token (only for write tools)

Reads and Keyword Planner work without it.

For writes (creating campaigns, keywords, ads), run a one-time Node script with `google-auth-library` — full snippet in **docs/INTEGRATIONS.md → Google Ads → Step 3**. Output is a `1//...` token; paste it.

integrations.label: Email (IMAP)
integrations.description: Read inbox via Gmail App Password / Zoho / custom IMAP — read-only by exposure.

fields.name: EMAIL_PROVIDER
fields.label: Provider
fields.helper: Pick a preset to auto-fill server settings, or Custom for a different IMAP host.

fields.name: EMAIL_HOST
fields.label: IMAP host
fields.helper: Your provider's IMAP server hostname.

fields.name: EMAIL_PORT
fields.label: Port
fields.helper: Usually 993 for IMAPS (encrypted).

fields.name: EMAIL_PASS
fields.label: Password
fields.helper: For Gmail / Workspace use an App Password (NOT your normal password). For Zoho / custom IMAP use your IMAP password.

fields.name: EMAIL_ID
fields.label: Account label (optional)
fields.helper: Short id used to refer to this account in chat (e.g. work, personal). Defaults to "primary".

fields.name: EMAIL_ALLOW_SEND
fields.label: Allow bot to send email on your behalf
fields.helper: Workspace-level setting that applies to every email account you add. When "no", the bot prepares drafts in your Drafts folder for you to review and send manually. Drafts always work; only outbound send is gated.

steps.title: Gmail only — App Password
steps.body:
Open [myaccount.google.com/apppasswords](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords) (requires 2-Step Verification on).

- Name it `{{botDisplayName}} IDE` → **Generate**
- Copy the **16-char password**, strip the spaces (they're visual only)

Skip this step for non-Gmail providers — just use your normal IMAP password.

steps.title: Pick the provider
steps.body:
Gmail and Zoho auto-fill server settings.

For anything else, pick **Custom IMAP** — you'll get fields for IMAP host + port (check your provider's IMAP help page).

steps.title: Fill the form

- **Email address** — the inbox you want to read

integrations.label: Google Analytics 4
integrations.description: Traffic, events, conversions, user behaviour — query GA4 metrics from chat.

fields.name: GA4_PROPERTY_ID
fields.label: Property ID
fields.helper: Plain number from Admin → Property Settings. NOT the Measurement ID (G-XXXX).

fields.name: GA4_CREDENTIALS_JSON_CONTENT
fields.label: Service account JSON

steps.title: Find your Property ID
steps.body:
[analytics.google.com](https://analytics.google.com) → **Admin** → **Property Settings** → copy **Property ID**.

It's a plain number like `123456789`. **Not** the Measurement ID `G-XXXXXXXX`.

steps.title: Create a service account
steps.body:
[console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com) → **IAM & Admin** → **Service Accounts** → **Create Service Account**.

Name it e.g. `mcp-{{botName}}`. No roles needed yet.

steps.title: Download the JSON key
steps.body:
Click the service account → **Keys** tab → **Add Key** → **Create new key** → **JSON** → **Create**.

A `.json` file downloads. Open it in a text editor and copy **the entire contents** — that's what goes in the field above.

steps.title: Grant the service account access in GA4
steps.body:
[analytics.google.com](https://analytics.google.com) → **Admin** → **Account Access Management** → **+** → **Add**.

- Email: copy `client_email` from the JSON (looks like `mcp-…@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com`)

integrations.label: GitHub
integrations.description: Read repos, issues, and pull requests via the official GitHub MCP server. Read-only by default; flip the toggle to let the bot commit, open PRs, and comment.

fields.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.label: Fine-grained PAT
fields.helper: Generate at github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new. Pick the repos this bot should see, then grant the permissions you need (Contents: Read or Read & write, Issues, Pull requests, Metadata). Token-level permissions are the outer security limit — the toggles below can only narrow them further.

fields.name: GITHUB_TOOLSETS
fields.label: Capabilities
fields.helper: Picks which groups of GitHub tools the bot exposes. Narrower = smaller attack surface and less context noise.

fields.name: GITHUB_ALLOW_WRITE
fields.label: Allow bot to modify repos

options.label: Yes — bot can commit, open PRs, comment

fields.helper: When "no", the MCP runs with --read-only and write tools are stripped before they reach the bot — it physically cannot modify anything even if it tried. Flip to "yes" only after you trust the bot's behaviour on a given repo. PAT-level scopes still apply on top: a read-only PAT will block writes regardless.

steps.title: Generate a fine-grained PAT
steps.body:
Open [github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new](https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new).

- **Token name**: `{{botDisplayName}} IDE`
- **Expiration**: 90 days (or custom)
- **Repository access**: pick the specific repos the bot should see — don't grant access to all repos
- **Repository permissions** (only what you need):
  - **Contents**: Read (or Read and write if you'll flip the write toggle)
  - **Issues**: Read / Read and write
  - **Pull requests**: Read / Read and write
  - **Metadata**: Read (auto-required)

Click **Generate token**, copy the `github_pat_…` string.

steps.title: Paste + pick the capabilities
steps.body: Paste the PAT above. Leave **Capabilities** on the recommended preset unless you need Actions / code security. Keep **Allow write = No** for the first few sessions — flip it later if you want the bot to push commits.

integrations.label: Trello
integrations.description: Read tasks, post, edit and delete comments, manage labels, move cards between columns, and attach or download files. The bot can pull a board's current state, comment on or tag a card, shift it to Done, drop a screenshot straight onto a card, or pull down files your team attached — all from chat.

fields.name: TRELLO_API_KEY
fields.label: API key
fields.helper: From your Trello Power-Up's API key page.

fields.name: TRELLO_TOKEN
fields.label: Token
fields.helper: Click the "Token" link under the API key (in the small paragraph that says "manually generate a Token"), authorise read + write, then paste the long string here. NOT the "Secret" field — that's for OAuth 1 and we don't use it.

fields.name: TRELLO_BOARDS
fields.label: Default boards
fields.helper: Optional. Easiest: paste the full board URL from your browser. For multiple boards, give each a friendly name: name:url,name:url. For a single board you can paste just the URL (or just the ID). The bot then accepts those names anywhere a board is asked for.

steps.title: Create a Power-Up + copy the API key
steps.body:
Open [trello.com/power-ups/admin](https://trello.com/power-ups/admin) → **New** → fill any name + workspace.

Open the new Power-Up → **API key** tab → **Generate**. Copy the **API key** (top field).

Ignore the **Secret** below it — that's for OAuth 1, we don't use it.

steps.title: Generate the Token
steps.body:
Same page, look for: *"…you can manually generate a Token."*

Click the word **Token** at the end. Authorise **read + write** → **Allow**. Copy the long string.

Do **not** paste the Secret from step 1.

steps.title: Optional — default boards
steps.body:
Paste a board URL from your browser, or for multiple, name them:

```
acme:https://trello.com/b/BFqnhhsY/acme,personal:https://trello.com/b/Other/me
```

Then the bot accepts "what's on acme?" instead of pasting URLs.

integrations.description: Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Drive, Slides, and Tasks — one OAuth refresh token unlocks all six. Writes are enabled by default and can be flipped off from the Settings cog.

fields.name: GDOCS_CLIENT_ID
fields.label: OAuth Client ID
fields.helper: From your own Google Cloud OAuth client (Web application type).

fields.name: GDOCS_CLIENT_SECRET
fields.label: OAuth Client Secret
fields.helper: Same OAuth client. Pair with the Client ID above.

fields.name: GDOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN
fields.label: Refresh token
fields.helper: Generate via OAuth Playground (instructions in step 3).

fields.name: GWORKSPACE_ALLOW_WRITE
fields.label: Allow bot to modify your Google Workspace data

options.label: Yes — bot can create / edit / delete (default)

fields.helper: Adds write permissions on top of read — bot can create, edit, and delete on your behalf.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client
steps.body:
[console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com) → **APIs & Services** → **Credentials** → **Create OAuth client ID** → **Web application**.

Authorised redirect URI: `https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground`

Save, then copy **Client ID** + **Client Secret** into the fields above.

steps.title: Enable the Workspace APIs
steps.body:
Same project → **APIs & Services** → **Library**. Enable every API in the bundle:

- **Google Docs API**
- **Google Drive API**
- **Google Sheets API**
- **Google Calendar API**
- **Google Slides API**
- **Google Tasks API**

Missing any of these → 403 from the corresponding tool.

steps.title: Generate the refresh token
steps.body:
Open [developers.google.com/oauthplayground](https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground) → **⚙ gear** (top right) → tick **Use your own OAuth credentials** → paste Client ID + Secret.

In **Step 1** (left side), paste **all** these scopes (one per line):

```
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/presentations
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/tasks
```

Click **Authorize APIs** → sign in with the Google account whose data the bot should see → **Allow**.

Then **Exchange authorization code for tokens** → copy the `refresh_token` (starts with `1//`).

integrations.label: Docs Comments
integrations.description: Lets your coworker drop inline comments anchored to a specific text range in a Google Doc — the one thing the Docs/Drive API can't do, so it drives a real logged-in Chromium session. You log in once through an embedded browser window; the session lives in a persistent container-side profile so later comment calls just work. Replying to, resolving, and deleting comments is handled separately by the Google Workspace integration over the Drive API (no browser needed).

fields.name: PROFILE_OK
fields.label: Google session
fields.helper: Click Connect to open an embedded Chromium window and sign in to Google. The session lives in a persistent profile under /var/wsapi-store/docs-comments-profile and is reused across container restarts.

steps.title: Click Connect to Google
steps.body: An embedded browser window opens in a modal. It's a real Chromium running inside the container — your normal Google login screen will appear (2FA, security key, whatever you have on).

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Use the account whose docs you want {{botDisplayName}} to comment on. The session — cookies, device-bound credentials, the lot — is saved to the container's persistent volume. Nothing leaves the server.

steps.title: Done
steps.body: Click Done in this dialog. The login Chromium is killed cleanly (so the profile flushes to disk), and the integration goes active. Subsequent add_comment tool calls reuse the saved session — no re-login until Google decides to rotate.

integrations.label: X (twitterapi.io)
integrations.description: Read tweets, profiles, replies, followers, mentions — full X data via twitterapi.io. Read-only by design; no X account credentials required, no developer approval, just a twitterapi.io API key.

fields.name: X_API_KEY
fields.label: twitterapi.io API key
fields.helper: From your twitterapi.io account → Dashboard. Pay-as-you-go: ~$0.15 per 1,000 tweets read.

steps.title: Sign up for twitterapi.io
steps.body:
Open [twitterapi.io](https://twitterapi.io) and create an account.

No X developer approval needed. You get **$0.10 free credit** to start (enough for ~600 tweets, plenty for testing).

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.body:
Dashboard → **API Keys** → copy the long alphanumeric string and paste it above.

This key only works against twitterapi.io — it has nothing to do with your actual X account.

integrations.label: Substack
integrations.description: Read public Substack content — list a publication's archive, read posts, look up authors, and follow Notes. No credentials needed; read-only.

steps.title: Just hit Activate
steps.body: No credentials needed — click Activate. The bot can then read any public Substack post, list a publication's archive, look up authors, and follow Notes. A `substack-research` skill installs automatically to help find and synthesise posts.
